_comment: Golden questions for the synthetic baseline mailbox (indexer/tests/baseline/corpus.py). Thread refs 'tNN' mean 'tNN.1@baseline.example'; message refs 'tNN.M' mean 'tNN.M@baseline.example'. required_evidence is a list of groups: every group is required, and any one thread in a group satisfies it. max_rank (1-based) bounds the first hit from any group; groups missing from the top 10 lower evidence recall instead. The recall floors are the hashed embedder's measured values rounded down: wiring checks, not semantic quality. vector_only questions must be answerable only by the vector lanes. unanswerable questions have no answer in the corpus: none of their absent_terms occurs in any message's subject, body or attachment (case-insensitive), and an abstaining agent must have asked for one of them. evidence_queries are get_evidence queries the outstanding-items reachability checks (#798, #907) and the OCR shape checks (#908, #1113) make; the build embeds them and they rank nothing in the snapshot. semantic questions are paraphrases sharing few words with their evidence; only the real-embedder run (make baseline-real-embedder, #1439) ranks them, against real_embedder_floors, which hold one independent floor per metric for each embedding model measured: synthetic regression evidence, not a mailbox-quality claim.

Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B._comment: make baseline-real-embedder, 2026-10-10, DeepInfra, batch size 64, queries sent one per request as mcp-server sends them, 5 repeats over all 73 search and semantic questions (#1439). Measured per repeat: hit_at_10 0.9589, mrr 0.8575-0.8587, evidence_recall_at_10 0.9384, multi_source_evidence_recall_at_10 0.7222. Between repeats 164 of 328 query vectors and 119 of 1,388 chunk vectors differed (max cosine distance 0.0031), moving 39 questions' top 10, and an earlier run with batched queries moved one question across rank 10. A second fresh five-repeat run, with chunk vectors cached per request, gave the same values. Each floor is the lowest repeat minus one question's worth (1/73 for hit, MRR and evidence recall; one group of a two-group question, 1/18, for multi-source recall), rounded down to two decimals: one question lost to variation passes, two fail.
